$comment: CROSS-REPO CONTRACT FIXTURE. The twin of this file lives in the backend repo
under the Playnite hash utils tests.
Both sides assert these digests against their own implementation of the
recipe. Either one drifting turns one suite red. Never re-baseline a digest to
make a test pass -- a changed digest means the two implementations no longer
agree, which is exactly the failure this file exists to catch.
`wire` is what System.Text.Json puts on the wire for a C# DateTime. `csharp`
is the canonical form that value must hash to on both sides:
The offset-bearing rows are the load-bearing ones. A Kind=Local DateTime
serializes with its offset, and that is the shape two independent normalizers
are most likely to disagree on. Vectors that only cover the already-canonical

dateNormalization.name: local negative offset with fractional seconds (production shape)
local negative offset, no fractional seconds (production shape)
local negative offset crossing into the next UTC day
utc with seven fractional digits (DateTime.ToString round-trip)

library.$comment: One game carrying realistic date shapes. Digests are asserted identically in both repos.
